items.headline: FDA approves first oral drug for dermatomyositis
items.summary: The FDA approved brepocitinib, sold as Lisraya, as the first pill for adults with dermatomyositis, a rare disease that causes muscle weakness and skin rash. In a year-long trial of two hundred forty one patients, it outperformed placebo on the disease's standard response measure.
items.why_it_matters: Patients with this rare autoimmune disease now have a first oral treatment option instead of relying only on injections or infusions.

items.headline: WHO prequalifies a new typhoid vaccine from South Korea's EuBiologics
items.summary: The World Health Organization granted prequalification to a new typhoid conjugate vaccine made by the South Korean company EuBiologics, clearing the way for United Nations agencies to buy it for immunization programs in developing countries. A trial of more than three thousand participants in Kenya and Senegal found it worked as well as an already approved vaccine.
items.why_it_matters: A second prequalified typhoid vaccine maker expands global supply and should help lower prices for the countries that need it most.
